results.name: Incline Bench Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position yourself in front of an incline bench.
Lean forward and place your hands on the incline bench, with your arms extended and your back straight parallel to the floor.
Push your hips back while keeping your hands on the bench, feeling the stretch in your back and hamstrings.
Repeat your hip motion, creating a dynamic stretch.
tips: Keep your back straight throughout the movement to ensure a proper stretch and prevent strain.
Focus on pushing your hips downwards rather than bending at the waist to enhance the stretch in your back.
Use controlled movements to avoid jerking or sudden motions that could lead to injury.
results.description: Incline Bench Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Back Stretch Standing With Bench
instructions: Stand tall near an incline bench with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms and reach the bench by leaning forward.
Hold the bench and extend your back while lowering your chest towards the floor.
Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your back.
tips: Engage your core muscles to maintain stability and support your lower back during the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down away from your ears to prevent tension.
Make sure your feet are firmly planted on the floor to provide a stable base and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Back Stretch Standing With Bench is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Back and Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Sit on a block with your back straight, feet shoulder-width apart and raise your right arm overhead.
Bend your right elbow and reach down your back. Use your left hand to gently pull on your right elbow, enhancing the stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Switch arms and repeat the stretch on the left side.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and proper posture throughout the stretch.
Avoid pulling too hard on your elbow; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Back and Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats.

results.name: Backward Abdominal Stretch
instructions: Get down on your knees with your back straight, thighs extended, and legs resting on the floor.
Lean backward and hold your feet by extending your arms to stretch your abdominal muscles.
Maintain this stretch for 30-60 seconds.
tips: Keep your hips stable to ensure a deep and effective stretch.
Avoid overextending your back; only lean as far back as is comfortable and safe for your flexibility.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Backward Abdominal Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your head in a neutral position.
Tilt your head backward, stretching the front of your neck.
Return to the neutral position, then tilt your head forward to stretch the back of your neck.
Turn your head to one side, holding briefly, and then return to the neutral position. Repeat on the other side.
tips: Perform the movements slowly and gently to avoid straining your neck muscles.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down to prevent tension in your upper back and shoulders.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Bent Arm Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your bent arm (elbow at a 90-degree angle) against the wall, with your forearm and hand flat against the wall.
Gently rotate your torso away from the wall to feel a stretch in your chest.
Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your shoulder down and away from your ear to avoid strain and ensure proper alignment.
Rotate your torso slowly to control the intensity of the stretch and prevent overstretching.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Bent Arm Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Biceps Stretch Behind the Back
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands together behind your back.
Straighten your arms and pull your shoulders back to feel a stretch in your biceps.
Keep your arms straight and maintain the stretch.
Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid arching to maintain proper form.
Ensure your hands are firmly clasped together to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Biceps Stretch Behind the Back is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Boat Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your knees slightly and lift your legs off the floor, balancing on your buttocks.
Extend your arms forward, parallel to the floor, to grab your legs and lean back slightly while keeping your back straight.
Hold this position, maintaining balance.
tips: Engage your core to maintain balance and prevent your lower back from rounding.
Keep your chest lifted and shoulders relaxed to ensure proper form.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help maintain the stretch and balance.
results.description: Boat Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Bodyweight Standing Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and bring both arms straight behind your back, holding your hands together.
Gently arch your back, pushing your hips forward and looking towards the ceiling.
Hold the stretched position for a few seconds, maintaining a gentle and controlled stretch.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the movement gentle to avoid straining your lower back.
Engage your core to support your lower back during the stretch.
Breathe deeply and steadily to enhance the stretch and relaxation.
results.description: Bodyweight Standing Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Chest.

results.name: Both Arms Behind on Wall Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand upright facing away from a wall and place both palms facing upward against it behind your body with your arms fully extended.
Bend your knees slowly while keeping your hands against the wall until you feel a gentle stretch in your upper arms and shoulders.
Keep your elbows fully extended, your chest up, and hold the stretch for the desired duration.
Return to starting position to release tension.
tips: Keep both elbows fully extended throughout the stretch.
Stand tall and avoid leaning your torso forward.
Bend your knees gradually, reaching a comfortable stretch without feeling pain.
Breathe slowly and evenly while holding the stretch.
results.description: Both Arms Behind on Wall Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Forearms.
